# Bison Algorithm

The goal here is, at first, compute the algorithm as it is written in the article.

## We import the data

```{r pressure, results = 'markup'}
data1 <- read_csv("/Users/enzobect/Documents/Bayesian-co-clustering-for-spatial-omics-data/Data/data_processed/mouse_brain_4700_bin_centers.csv")

data2 <- read_csv("/Users/enzobect/Documents/Bayesian-co-clustering-for-spatial-omics-data/Data/data_processed/mouse_brain_top500_4700bins_vals.csv")




head(data2, 10)
```

## Model formulation

The goal here is to simulate $(Y_{ij} \mid Z_i = k, W_j = r) \sim \text{Poisson}(s_i*g_j*\mu_{rk})$.

$s_i = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^W y_{ij}}{\sum_{j=1}^W \sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}$.

$g_j = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}{\sum_{j=1}^W \sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}$.

$\mu_{rk} \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha_{\mu},\beta_{\mu})$ where $\alpha_{\mu} = \beta_{\mu} = 1$. So, $\mu_{rk} \sim \text{Exp}(\lambda)$ where $\lambda = 1$

This is the exact simulation but ...

```{r pressure, results = 'markup'}



si<- rowSums(data2)/sum(data2) # s is a vector st s[i] = si
s_tot<-sum(si) #we normalize the si, tiw s_tot = 1

wj<- colSums(data2) 
gj<-wj/sum(data2)# g is a vector st g[j] = gj

u = runif(1)
lambda<-1
mu_rk<-(-1/lambda)*log(u) # we simulate exp_law
print(mu_rk)

poisson_lambda <- outer(si, gj, "*") * mu_rk

max(poisson_lambda)

y<-rpois(n=length(s) * length(g),lambda = poisson_lambda)
head(y,50)
```

The problem here is the quantity $s_i*g_j*\mu_{rk} \sim 10^{-5}$ is too low. Then $(Y_{ij} \mid Z_i = k, W_j = r) = 0$ for each simulation.

So, I tried to simulate with different values of $g_j$ : $g_j = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}{N_{genes}}$, $g_j = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}{\sqrt{N_{genes}}}$, $g_j = \sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}$. Therefore, the difference is the meaning of $g_j$ :

$g_j = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}{N_{spot}}$ means "On average, this gene produces 12 molecules by spot on the tissue".

$g_j = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}{\sum_{j=1}^W \sum_{i=1}^N y_{ij}}$ means "the ratio of the presence of this gene on the tissue according to the presence of the others ones".

```{r pressure, results='markup'}

si<- rowSums(data2)/sum(data2) # s is a vector st s[i] = si
N<-ncol(data2)
s_tot<-sum(si) #we normalize the si, tiw s_tot = 1

wj<- colSums(data2) 
W<-nrow(data2)
gj<-wj
gj2<-wj/W**0.5
#gj3<-wj/W

u = runif(1)
lambda<-1
mu_rk<-(-1/lambda)*log(u) # we simulate exp_law
print(mu_rk)

poisson_lambda <- outer(si, gj, "*") * mu_rk
poisson_lambda2 <- outer(si, gj2, "*") * mu_rk
#poisson_lambda3 <- outer(si, gj3, "*") * mu_rk

max(poisson_lambda)

y_sim <- matrix(
  rpois(n = length(poisson_lambda), lambda = poisson_lambda),
  nrow = W,
  ncol = N
)

y_sim2 <- matrix(
  rpois(n = length(poisson_lambda2), lambda = poisson_lambda2),
  nrow = W,
  ncol = N
)



palette_couleurs <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100)

pheatmap(
  log2(y_sim + 1),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  main = "Matrix (échelle log2)"
)

pheatmap(
  log2(y_sim2 + 1),
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  show_rownames = FALSE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  main = "Matrix 2 (échelle log2)"
)

#  show_rownames = FALSE,
#  show_colnames = FALSE,
#  main = "Matrix 3 (échelle log2) "
#)


```

We search, how similar is the distribution of the genes according to both of the $g_j$.

Spoiler : we remark that the top 10 is similar and is is also similar to the real data.

```{r pressure, results = 'markup'}

g_sim<-colSums(y_sim)
g_sim2<-colSums(y_sim2)

top_5_real_data <- order(wj, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
top5 <- order(g_sim, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
top5_2 <- order(g_sim2, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

top_5_real_data
top5
top5_2

bottom_real_data <- order(wj)[1:10]
bottom <- order(g_sim)[1:10]
bottom_2 <- order(g_sim2)[1:10]

g_sim[bottom]
g_sim[bottom_2]

```

Conclusion : In that way, we can say by using both of the $g_j$, the local probability to draw the gene $j$ on the spot $i$ is depended on the block $\mu_{rk}$ .

## Prior on spot (Potts model or MRF ? )

$P(z)$

## Prior on gene (Zero-inflated Polya urn prior)

$P(w) = \pi_0^{w_{0}}*(1-\pi_0)^{w-w_{0}}* \frac{\gamma^R*\prod_{r=1}^R{\text{Gamma}(w_r)}}{\prod_{j=1}^{w-w_0}(\gamma+j-1)}$ where $\pi_{0} \sim \beta(\alpha_\pi,\beta_\pi)$ . Gamma depends on the number of spots in the data and the number of cluster K that we want to reach. If gamma increases the probability of a new cluster increases too.

```{r pressure, results = 'markup'}

gamma_parameter<-c(0.1,0.2,0.5,1,2,5)

# alpha_pi = beta_pi = 1 donc suit une loi uniforme 
pi_0<-runif(1)

      



```

## Posterior inference

$P(\mu,w,z \mid Y ) \propto P(Y \mid \mu,w,z)*P(\mu \mid w,z)*P(z)*P(w)$
